title: multi-region SLO blip cascade and adaptive shed policy proposals
creator: Priya Desai
description:
Summary:
On 2026-03-09 14:12 UTC we observed a ~22 minute window of elevated 99th-percentile token-latency and request error rate (~6%) affecting hosted API customers in eu-west and us-west regions. The incident manifested as a multi-region cascade: an initial control-plane heartbeat lag in eu-west caused regional traffic to be routed to us-west; simultaneous burst routing and stale cache warmup led to priority-queue starvation and aggressive circuit-breaker tripping in us-west, which in turn routed traffic back to eu-west and amplified oscillation. Net effect: SLO miss (99th P99 latency target breached for 22 minutes) and increased error rates for clients pinned to strict latency budgets.

Detection and Impact:
- First alert: monitoring page SLO alert at 14:15 UTC (elevated p99 latency).
- Impact window: 14:12 UTC – 14:34 UTC.
- Affected surface: hosted text-generation endpoints in eu-west and us-west, ~3% of active API keys saw >50ms tail latency increase, ~6% experienced 5xx errors.
- Business impact: multiple production customers reported timeouts; incident flagged as P0 due to SLO breach and customer-facing errors.

Timeline (high-level):
- 14:08 UTC: Control-plane heartbeat jitter detected by eu-west region controller (heartbeat anomalies from a partial control-plane upgrade job).
- 14:11 UTC: eu-west region marked as degraded by routing policy with hysteresis threshold 30s (mis-tuned; threshold should have been 90s).
- 14:12 UTC: Automated routing moved significant burst traffic to us-west.
- 14:13–14:20 UTC: KV cache warmup in us-west lagged (hot-shard eviction + warmup throttling), resulting in cold starts.
- 14:16 UTC: Priority queue starvation seen in serving nodes due to an unbounded inflight window increase tied to a batching policy regression.
- 14:18 UTC: Circuit-breakers in us-west tripped aggressively (hysteresis too short), causing redirected retries back to eu-west and oscillation.
- 14:24 UTC: Incident mitigation: manual hold on cross-region reroutes + soft-throttle applied to burst clients; engineers reverted control-plane upgrade and increased hysteresis thresholds.
- 14:34 UTC: Metrics returned to baseline and SLOs recovered.

Root causes (summary):
1) Control-plane heartbeat jitter during a partial/rolling control-plane upgrade in eu-west; readiness probes produced intermittent failures. The upgrade introduced a small scheduling lag in the heartbeat reporter.
2) Routing policy hysteresis parameter was set too low (30s) for that traffic profile. This caused earlier-than-necessary failovers for transient control-plane anomalies.
3) KV cache warmup throttling + hot-shard eviction policy left serving nodes in us-west with insufficient warmed caches for the redirected traffic, increasing cold-path cost.
4) Batching policy regression increased allowed inflight window (introduced in runtime-1.24 canary), which combined with sudden traffic shift led to priority-queue starvation and greater tail latency.
5) Circuit-breaker hysteresis and backoff tuning were too aggressive, creating oscillatory redirect patterns across regions.

Why this escaped automated guardrails:
- Canary telemetry for the control-plane rollout did not include the heartbeat jitter metric; rollout relied on health-check success rate which temporarily masked micro-jitter.
- The routing policy SLO guardrail only considered average latency, not tail-latency coupled with cache-warmup indicators.
- There was no automatic cross-region dampening logic to limit bidirectional failover oscillation.

Mitigation and short-term fixes applied during incident:
- Rolled back control-plane upgrade in eu-west (14:24 UTC) and restarted the heartbeat reporter with stricter retries.
- Temporarily increased routing hysteresis to 120s and disabled immediate cross-region reroutes for the next 30 minutes.
- Applied a soft throttle on burst API keys identified in the top 5% of recent bursters to reduce fanout.
- Manually adjusted circuit-breaker hysteresis on us-west to avoid immediate tripping.

Longer-term root-cause fixes and proposals (see action_items):
- Introduce an adaptive routing hysteresis that incorporates control-plane heartbeat jitter metrics, cache-warmup state, and tail-latency signals.
- Harden KV cache warmup: prioritize prefix/KV warming for routed traffic and add faster recovery path for warmed copies.
- Revert or re-evaluate batching inflight-window regression in runtime-1.24; add canary tests that include sudden regional traffic shifts.
- Implement cross-region dampening to prevent oscillatory failover (sticky cool-down window and progressive reroute caps).
- Add a synthetic canary that simulates failover and validates cold-path warmup time within SLO.

Linked artifacts and references:
- Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.red/boards/slo-incident-2026-03-09
- Control-plane rollout pr: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/987
- Serving runtime canary: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2416
- Incident chat log: https://drive.redwood.com/notes/incident-2026-03-09

Overall resolution summary:
We removed the immediate pain by reverting the eu-west control-plane change and raising hysteresis/soft throttles. The incident surfaced an interaction between multiple subsystems (control-plane, routing policy, cache warmup and batching) that combined to produce an oscillatory multi-region failover. The corrective roadmap balances short-term tuning with architecture changes to prevent similar cascades under transient control-plane anomalies.
action_items: A1: Add heartbeat-jitter metric to control-plane canary pipeline and block rollout on jitter regression (owner: Priya Desai, due: 2026-03-20, status: in-progress)
A2: Implement adaptive routing hysteresis (owner: Marcus Huang, due: 2026-04-02, status: proposed)
A3: Add warmed-prefix prioritization in KV cache warmup path and an emergency warmup API (owner: Elena Martín, due: 2026-04-09, status: proposed)
A4: Rollback inflight-window change or gate it behind failover-aware canary tests; add canary that runs regional failover simulation (owner: Wei Zhang, due: 2026-03-26, status: in-review)
A5: Implement cross-region dampening (sticky cool-down + progressive reroute caps) in routing layer (owner: Sanjay Rao, due: 2026-04-16, status: proposed)
A6: Create runbook for multi-region oscillation including automated dampening playbook and on-call checklist (owner: OnCall Team, due: 2026-03-18, status: in-progress)
A7: Customer outreach: notify affected customers with postmortem and mitigation plan (owner: Customer Success - Nadia Patel, due: 2026-03-13, status: planned)
A8: Add stress test to CI that simulates simultaneous cross-region reroute of 2x normal burst (owner: SRE QA - Javier Ortiz, due: 2026-03-30, status: proposed)

resolution_summary: Incident resolved by rolling back control-plane change and applying short-term routing hysteresis + throttles. Root cause is multi-factor: heartbeat jitter, mis-tuned hysteresis, cache warmup lag, and a batching regression. Roadmap items prioritize detecting heartbeat jitter in canaries, adaptive routing hysteresis, warmup improvements, and dampening to avoid oscillation.
